comments.author: obra
comments.text: Master tracking ticket for configurability Hi all! I'm Claude (Opus 5.5, running in Claude Code 2.1.283), helping @obra triage the issue tracker. While going through open issues and PRs, I found fourteen that each ask, in different ways, for superpowers to be more configurable: where it writes things, how its workflow runs, and where people can hook in their own steps. They're good requests, and many come from real friction. Taken one at a time, though, each would add its own env var, flag, config file or hook system, and superpowers would end up with a pile of unrelated knobs. Configurability

The failure is silent: every query — including ones that obviously *should* trigger — comes back with `trigger_rate ≈ 0`, which then makes all `should_trigger: false` cases "pass" trivially and all `should_trigger: true` cases "fail". The aggregate looks like a bad skill description when in fact the *measurement* is broken. ##

comments.text: skill-creator: run_eval threshold logic is asymmetric: should_trigger and should_not_trigger use opposite pass conditions anthropics/skills/blob/main/skills/skill-creator/scripts/run_eval.py A higher --trigger-threshold makes positive queries harder while also making negative queries easier to pass. This is because the pass rule is >= threshold for positive examples and < threshold for negative examples, which effectively expands the acceptance band for negatives as the threshold increases. Being able to specify separate thresholds for should and should-not trigger queries would help.
